claims.text: The as-built additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has a uniform FCC matrix.
The starting alloy has demonstrated strong fatigue performance.
High-temperature degradation in this alloy is governed by selective surface diffusion and oxidation of Al and Ti.
Under oxidizing conditions, Al and Ti preferentially diffuse to the alloy surface.
Surface-segregated Al and Ti selectively oxidize to form a thin, adherent, mixed oxide scale.
The proposed protective scale consists primarily of Al2O3 and may incorporate TiO2.
The mixed oxide scale acts as a barrier that slows further oxidation.
Formation of the proposed oxide scale preserves the integrity of the FCC matrix.
Under reducing or low-oxygen conditions, protective surface-scale formation is suppressed.
Suppression of the protective scale under reducing conditions promotes internal oxidation.
Reducing-condition exposure promotes the nucleation or coalescence of vacancies, voids, or related defects.
Internal oxidation and defect formation under reducing conditions degrade mechanical properties.
The diffusion kinetics of Al and Ti within the FCC matrix govern whether a coherent protective scale forms.
Oxidizing exposure at 900–1100 °C will produce a coherent, continuous, chemically passivating surface scale with minimal subsurface degradation.
Reducing exposure at 900–1100 °C will produce minimal or discontinuous surface oxide.
Reducing exposure will produce internal oxidation and porous microstructural features.
Reducing exposure will cause localized phase decomposition.
The proposed mechanism applies to clean-gas exposures between 900 °C and 1100 °C for durations sufficient for steady-state diffusion and scale development or suppression.
Post-processing that changes diffusion kinetics or phase stability may move the alloy outside the proposed mechanism's applicability.
